coverage_note: Read the whole supplied transcript. Several stretches are English-only or contain Latin-transliterated Arabic; chat was used for context, not as a correction by itself. Pronunciation slips such as سجر for فجر were excluded under S4. The referenced echo-candidates file was not supplied; the transcript itself appears to render his Arabic echo at 44:20 as “El nar, nar heret me.” Medi Arabic-turn count is approximate because many short turns mix Arabic and English.

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme

Amal asks what سنان means; he answers ‘teeth’, and she supplies سنين for years.

rows.amal_said: Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.

rows.why: Amal prompts ‘it’ as the missing object, after which he adds -ha and she voices نظفتها.
In his list of things on the land, Amal appears to prompt plural وردات—the engine writes وحدات—and he responds وردات؟

rows.medi_said: Is it... Is it the bee? Is it the bee plants?
rows.amal_said: Z-z-zبيب is raisins, I think. Is... زريعة.
rows.why: He searches for the Arabic word for plants in English, and Amal eventually supplies زريعة; زبيب is her intervening guess at what she heard.
Looking for dirt or soil, he tries رمل; Amal identifies it as sand, then confirms his subsequent تراب as dirt or soil.

rows.medi_said: I don't, أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: Asked for ‘stones’, he says he does not know the word, and Amal supplies حجر.
Amal changes his singular street to plural الشوارع for the old streets he goes on to describe.
rows.english: The old streets in America are stone.

rows.why: Amal adds الـ to the adjective describing the definite الشوارع; he repeats الإدام afterward.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. Made of is different than made.
rows.proposed_rule: To describe something as made of a material, the material can be the predicate: الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر, not عملت مع حجر.
rows.why: Amal replaces ‘made with stone’ with ‘are stone’ and explicitly distinguishes ‘made of’ from ‘made’; no listed bucket precisely states this material-predicate construction.
rows.english: The old streets in America are made of stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.chat: the second stone was my favorite
rows.why: For ‘the second stone’, Amal restores his earlier تاني حجر and also offers الحجر التاني; حجر تاني changes the sense toward another stone.
rows.english: The second stone was my favorite.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Amal supplies المفضل عندي for ‘my favorite’ standing after the stone, instead of his possessive ending on the adjective.
rows.english: The second stone was my favorite.

rows.medi_said: مفضل-- مفضل عندي أو مفضل لي يعني؟
rows.why: After the first correction he again omits الـ, and Amal explicitly prompts and voices المفضل عندي.

rows.medi_said: Yeah، okay. So الـ حجري الـ مفضل.
rows.why: Amal explicitly removes the article before حجري, which already carries its possessive owner ending.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders.
rows.why: In this new lesson example he again omits الـ, and Amal says al-mufaddal and gives the full sentence at 58:45.
